messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Launch day traffic spike — temporary quota increase?

Hi Jasmine,

Quick question as we lock down the launch day runbook: our engineering team expects a short peak (~6 hours) on Sept 2 UTC where API calls to your defaultroute will spike to ~1.8x our trial levels — roughly 180M tokens over that window. Is there a way to provision a temporary quota/throughput bump (or short-term dedicated pool) for that window? We're on the annual pilot (deal ACME-EXP-2026-07) and happy to sign any addendum.

Attached is our latest forecast for the launch (acme_traffic_forecast_v3.xlsx).

Thanks — Samir
Samir Khan
Director, Launch Operations
ACME Health

Team — looping you all in for a quick cadence on ACME Health's Sept 2 launch. Samir pasted their ask above and included the forecast. TL;DR: they expect a ~1.8x spike for ~6 hours (estimate: 180M tokens in-slot). As their AE on the pilot, I want to coordinate:

- Product: what constraints do we have on short-duration quota bumps versus provisioning a dedicated burst pool?
- Capacity/infra: can we guarantee the throughput with their current plan if we temporarily increase quota? If not, what's required (lead time, costs, failover plan)?
- Reliability: any risk of cross-customer impact if we temporarily bump them? If so, how do we isolate?

Desired outcome this week: decision on whether we can offer a one-off quota uplift + precise numbers / cost estimate so I can get Samir's sign-off and DocuSign in place.

Samir — can you confirm the 6-hour window (start/end in UTC) and the expected 95th percentile requests per second (RPS) or tokens/sec? Your spreadsheet has per-minute buckets but if you can give an hourly P95 that'd help.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-11T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch day traffic spike — temporary quota increase?

Thanks for the ping, Jasmine. Quick notes from product/runtime:

- We can support a temporary quota uplift as a "burst entitlement" for hosted customers, but it depends on two things: slot capacity availability in the chosen region (us-east-1) and whether the traffic profile is bursty (many concurrent short requests) vs. sustained high tokens/sec.
- For a 6 hour window with ~180M tokens, rough compute estimate is ~3.6 GPU-hours on a T4-equivalent baseline if the workload is primarily generation with average token length similar to what their forecast shows. If their requests are conversational with long context, that can double.
- If they need stronger latency SLOs we should consider a temporary dedicated pool (reserved instances for 24 hours) — that has higher cost but isolates impact.

Questions for Samir (cc'd):
1) Can you send an hourly P95 tokens/sec or RPS for Sept 2 UTC?
2) Are you using streaming responses heavily?
3) Do you have a preferred region?

If they can give hourly P95 it's straightforward to map to batching/slot sizing and give a firm answer.

— Dev
Product, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Launch day traffic spike — temporary quota increase?

Checked regional capacity against planned maintenance and other reserved bursts — here's what we can do:

- We can grant a temporary quota uplift for ACME Health in us-east-1 covering the Sept 2 00:00-06:00 UTC window to support the projected P95s.
- Proposed configuration: increase their token-per-minute quota and add a burst entitlement that increases concurrent slot allotment by 2x for that window.
- Costing: we will bill as a short-term reserved burst at MSRP + 12% premium; estimate for the 6 hour window based on Dev's comp estimates and their streaming fraction = $4,800.
- Requirements: final confirmation by EOD Aug 14, and we need the signed addendum (Samir attached it — thanks). Also need a fallback route: if latency or errors exceed our SLOs during the window, we will automatically throttle back to their baseline and alert the on-call.

Action items:
- Jasmine: confirm with Samir the final acceptance of cost and the precise start/end timestamps (we have 00:00-06:00 UTC).
- Dev: please map the P95 numbers to exact slot counts and confirm if any model variants will need pinning.
- Dylan: please add a temporary routing rule and set the automatic fallback threshold.
- Neha/Aditya: please log the entitlement in quota system and prepare billing note.

— Laura
Director, Capacity & Dedicated Product

Mapping complete: based on the P95 tokens/sec and 30% streaming, we recommend the following slot profile for the 00:00-06:00 UTC window:
- Baseline slots: 6
- Burst slots during peak: +8 slots (total 14) from 02:00-04:00 UTC, scaled down to +4 the surrounding hours.
- Model pinning: pin their route to the "redwood-1.8-opt" variant for that window to avoid cold-start regressions.
- Expected compute: ~4.2 GPU-hours (higher than initial estimate due to streaming).

I will push the slot assignment to the orchestration and notify infra. Laura — your cost estimate looks good; Neha/Aditya please confirm billing code. Dylan — please set the fallback if error rate >1.2% sustained for 3 minutes.

— Dev

Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and the signed addendum. To confirm back to you:

- We will provision a temporary burst entitlement for ACME Health in us-east-1 for Sept 2, 2026 from 00:00-06:00 UTC.
- Peak slot configuration: total 14 slots between 02:00-04:00 UTC; lower burst levels the other hours per Dev's mapping.
- Cost: $4,800 (short-term reserved burst). We'll issue an invoice post-window.
- Safety: automatic fallback will throttle to baseline if error rates exceed thresholds; our on-call will monitor and can escalate.

Please reply with a one-line OK and I'll mark the ticket and entitlement complete. Also, Samir — if any of the timestamps slide, please give us 48-hour heads-up.

Thanks all for the fast coordination.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
